title: Internal Hom and scalar localization under sequential continuity
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, and assume that filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the relative derived tensor product [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex], and ambient derived internal Hom $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $s$ be a global section of $R$ and put $S=R[1/s]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization], whose underlying $R$-module is the telescope $\varinjlim(R\xrightarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{s}\cdots)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization]. Let $K\in D(R)$ have the following property: for every sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ of complexes of $R$-module sheaves with one common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced comparison
$$\varinjlim_n H_R(K,M_n^\bullet)\longrightarrow H_R(K,\varinjlim_n M_n^\bullet)$$
is an isomorphism; filtered colimits here are exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial complex representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Then for every $L\in D(R)$ whose cohomology vanishes in sufficiently negative degrees the canonical evaluation-transpose map
$$S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\longrightarrow H_S(S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(S)$, natural in $K,L$. Its restriction to $D(R)$, under the evaluation-normalized scalar adjunction, is the sequential-continuity isomorphism $S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\simeq H_R(K,S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}L)$. No constructibility, completeness, or perfectness hypothesis is imposed beyond the displayed continuity assumption.

proof.text: Choose $a$ with $H^i(L)=0$ for $i<a$ and a complex $M$ representing $L$. Replace $M$ by $P$: put $P^i=0$ for $i<a$, $P^a=\operatorname{coker}(d_M^{a-1})$, and $P^i=M^i$ for $i>a$, with the induced differential. The quotient map $M\to P$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at least $a$ and maps zero to zero below $a$; it is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the constant sequence $P\xrightarrow{s}P\xrightarrow{s}\cdots$ has one termwise lower bound, as required by the continuity hypothesis.

proof.text: Write $E(M)=S\otimes_R M$ and let $U_0$ be restriction of scalars. Scalar localization is exact by the cited exactness theorem; $U_0$ is exact by the cited coefficient adjunction. Applying them termwise gives $F:D(R)\to D(S)$ and $U:D(S)\to D(R)$. Identify $F$ with $S\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}-$: the K-flat formula for derived change of rings and exactness identify both on a resolution $Q\to M$, since $E(Q)\to E(M)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The normalized derived coefficient adjunction gives $F\dashv U$, with unit $\eta_A:A\to UFA$ induced by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$.

proof.text: For any complex $N$ of $S$-modules, multiplication $EU_0N\to N$, $b\otimes x\mapsto bx$, is inverse to $x\mapsto1\otimes x$: locally $s^{-n}\otimes x=1\otimes s^{-n}x$, by multiplying by the invertible $s^n$ and balancing. These equalities sheafify and commute with differentials. The normalized derived counit $\varepsilon_N:FUN\to N$ is therefore an isomorphism. Consequently precomposition with $\eta_A$ bijects maps $UFA\to UN$ with maps $A\to UN$: its inverse sends $h$ to $U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(h)$. To check uniqueness directly, $UF\eta_A=\eta_{UFA}$ since both are inverse to $U\varepsilon_{FA}$; naturality of $\eta$ and $U\varepsilon_N\circ\eta_{UN}=1$ give $q=U\varepsilon_N\circ UF(q\circ\eta_A)$ for every $q:UFA\to UN$.

source.place: Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), normalization; elementary localization multiplication and the two adjunction triangle identities

proof.text: Apply the complex-colimit theorem with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z[T]$, $t=T$, acting through the global section $s$. For every complex $B$, without a lower-bound assumption, it identifies the termwise colimit of $B\xrightarrow{s}B\to\cdots$ with $U_0E(B)$; its $n$th leg represents $U(s^{-n})\eta_{QB}$. Exactness of filtered colimits implies that they preserve quasi-isomorphisms (cohomology is kernel modulo image), so the same identifications hold for the functorial representatives stipulated in the statement. In particular they apply both to $P$ and to a representative of $H_R(K,L)$, even when that internal Hom is unbounded below.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits) and Section 03EK; complex-colimit telescope and its normalized legs

proof.text: Represent $K$ by $\mathcal L$ and put $X=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L,I(P))$, the Hom-complex defining $H_R(K,L)$ with the fixed functorial K-injective resolution $i:P\to I(P)$. Applying $H_R(K,-)$ to the scalar tower on $P$ gives the tower $X\xrightarrow{t_1}X\to\cdots$ with $t_1=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L,I(s))$; the scalar tower on $X$ has $t_2=s$, and postcomposition by $s$ is multiplication by $s$ on every component, $s\varphi=s\circ\varphi$. The maps $I(s)$ and $s_{I(P)}$ satisfy $Q(I(s))Q(i)=Q(i)Q(s_P)=Q(s_{I(P)})Q(i)$ with $Q(i)$ invertible, so they agree in $D(R)$ and, $I(P)$ being K-injective, are homotopic by the cited bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_K\to\operatorname{Hom}_D$; postcomposing a homotopy $h$ gives $t_1-t_2=dh'+h'd$ on $X$. Each termwise sequential colimit is the cokernel of the termwise monomorphism $f_k=1-\sigma_{t_k}:\bigoplus_nX\to\bigoplus_nX$ ($\iota_n\mapsto\iota_n-\iota_{n+1}t_k$), with the $n$th leg induced by $\iota_n$. Since $f_1-f_2=dH+Hd$ for $H=-\sigma_{h'}$, the map $(x,y)\mapsto(x,y+Hx)$ is an isomorphism of mapping cones $\operatorname{cone}(f_1)\cong\operatorname{cone}(f_2)$ which is the identity on the second summand; and $(x,y)\mapsto[y]$, $\operatorname{cone}(f_k)\to\operatorname{coker}f_k$, is a quasi-isomorphism because its kernel is isomorphic to $\operatorname{cone}(1_{\bigoplus X})$, which is contractible. Hence the colimits of the two towers are isomorphic in $D(R)$ compatibly with every leg. Apply precisely the assumed sequential-continuity comparison to the bounded-below input tower $(P,s)$ of step 1, and step 4 to the tower $(X,s)$ and to $(P,s)$. This gives an isomorphism $\beta:UFH_R(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(K,UFL)$. Its composite with $\eta_{H_R(K,L)}$ is $H_R(K,\eta_L)$, because the continuity comparison is induced by evaluation, the leg-compatible isomorphism above preserves the zeroth leg, and the zeroth colimit leg is the unit. No lower bound on $H_R(K,L)$ has been used.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12 and Proposition 6.8.14(2), pp. 61–62; agent conditional specialization, using the stated internal-sheaf continuity hypothesis rather than global Hom continuity

proof.text: Let $\chi:FH_R(K,L)\to H_S(FK,FL)$ be the canonical evaluation-transpose map in the statement, and let $\alpha:UH_S(FK,FL)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_R(K,UFL)$ be the cited evaluation-normalized scalar-Hom isomorphism. Their normalization gives $(\alpha\circ U\chi)\circ\eta_{H_R(K,L)}=H_R(K,\eta_L)$: transposing either side gives evaluation $K\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(K,L)\to L$ followed by $\eta_L$, since $\chi$ is the transpose of extended evaluation and $\alpha$ uses the scalar unit on $K$. The target is isomorphic via $\alpha$ to $UN$ for $N=H_S(FK,FL)$. The uniqueness proved in step 3 therefore gives $\alpha\circ U\chi=\beta$. This establishes equality of the actual derived maps, not just their values on the individual telescope legs.

source.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); agent application of evaluation normalization and scalar-unit uniqueness

proof.text: Since $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are isomorphisms, so is $U\chi$. The conservativity assertion of the scalar-Hom adjunction node implies that $\chi$ is an isomorphism in $D(S)$. Step 6 also identifies its restriction with the asserted sequential-continuity isomorphism. Naturality in $L$ and contravariant naturality in $K$ (among objects satisfying the displayed continuity assumption) follow from the functorial evaluation map defining $\chi$ and the natural isomorphism $\alpha$; the representative and colimit choices do not alter this canonical map.
